q: What is the most common type of faux leather material?
n: PU (polyurethane) leather is the most common faux leather today. It is softer and more breathable than PVC leather. Source: Textile industry references on synthetic leather; ASTM D2208 (Leather Testing).

q: What is the most damaging factor to synthetic leather when it comes to maintenance?
o: Occasional use of mild cleaning agents
n: Prolonged exposure to direct sunlight is the most damaging factor to synthetic leather because it causes the material to dry out, crack, fade, and lose its elasticity. UV rays degrade the synthetic coating and weaken the fibers, leading to premature aging and deterioration. !n contrast, occasional use of mild cleaning agents is generally safe when used properly, as they help maintain cleanliness without damaging the surface. Routine application of leather conditioner can actually prolong the life of synthetic leather by keeping it supple and preventing dryness. Consistent indoor temperature control has minimal impact since synthetic leather is relatively stable under normal indoor conditions. Therefore, while cleaning and conditioning are beneficial, sunlight exposure remains the primary threat to synthetic leather's longevity. Prolonged direct sunlight (UV and heat) degrades synthetic leather. The coating fades, dries out and cracks. Source: Manufacturers' care guides for PU/PVC upholstery; ASTM D4329 (UV Exposure of Plastics).

q: Which application is a tile with a grip finish best suited for?
n: Grip finish tiles are designed to provide slip resistance, making them ideal for outdoor patios or areas prone to moisture, where safety is a priority. Tiles with grip (anti-slip) finishes are made for wet exterior floors such as patios, pool decks and ramps. Source: ANSI A137.1 (DCOF slip resistance); Tile Council of North America Handbook.

q: "Salt and pepper” is a common pattern of which floor tile?
n: Salt and pepper granite tiles are characterized by their distinctive speckled pattern, created by a combination of light and dark mineral crystals, making them popular for flooring and countertops. "Salt and pepper" is the speckled black-and-white look of granite tiles, from mixed light and dark minerals. Source: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual (Granite).

q: Which of the following is typically the most expensive type of marble?
n: Bookmatched marble is typically the most expensive due to the complex process of aligning consecutive slabs to create a mirrored, symmetrical pattern, making it highly sought after for luxurious interior designs. Bookmatched marble costs more because consecutive slabs must be cut, selected and laid as mirror images. That increases waste and labor. Source: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual (Bookmatching).

q: Who is responsible to produce the record drawings?
n: Record drawings are also known as as-built drawings. The contractor produces record (as-built) drawings that show the work as actually constructed. The architect may review them. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 301 (General Conditions – Record Drawings); Architect's Guidelines (2016).

q: Where is a pipe sleeve typically required?
n: Pipe sleeves are cast into slabs and walls where pipes pass through. They allow movement and replacement, and penetrations can then be firestopped. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Sleeves); ASTM E814 (Firestop Systems).

q: Which construction method involves creating a reinforced concrete wall by excavating a trench stabilized with slurry before pouring concrete?
n: A slurry wall is formed by excavating a trench supported with bentonite slurry, then replacing the slurry with concrete. It is ideal for deep excavations, especially in urban settings, to manage groundwater and soil pressure. A slurry (diaphragm) wall is cast in a trench excavated under bentonite slurry, which holds the trench open until concrete is tremied in. Source: Das, Principles of Foundation Engineering (Diaphragm Walls); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 3.

q: In prestressed concrete, what method is used to offset or counteract the weight of the structure using the force from tendons?
n: Load balancing uses the force from prestressed tendons to counter the structure’s own weight, helping reduce deflection and improve performance. In the load-balancing method of prestressed concrete design, draped tendons exert upward forces that counteract part of the gravity load. Source: Lin & Burns, Design of Prestressed Concrete Structures (Load Balancing); Nawy, Prestressed Concrete.

q: Minimum main rebars for a spiral column.
n: Spirally reinforced columns need at least 6 longitudinal bars. Tied rectangular columns need 4. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 410.7.3.1 (Minimum number of longitudinal bars); ACI 318.

q: What is an ideal task lighting on the kitchen counter?
n: Under-cabinet strip lighting puts light right on the counter without shadows from the user's head. It is the ideal kitchen task lighting. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Residential Kitchen Lighting).

q: What is the maximum occupant load for the session hall according to the building code?
n: In places of assembly, the occupant load for areas without fixed seats such as an auditorium is 0.65sqm/person. The area of the session hall is 337.5sqm so the occupant load is 337.5sqm/0.65 = 519.23 or 520 people. Assembly areas without fixed seats use 0.65 sqm per person: 337.5 sqm / 0.65 = 520 persons. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Occupant Load Factors – Assembly); NFPA 101, Table 7.3.1.2.
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 5 – 2-STOREY PROVINCIAL CAPITOL BUILDING

Design Problem. The Provincial Government of Occidental Mindoro, headquartered in the capital town of Mamburao, has long operated from an aging capitol complex that no longer meets the spatial, functional, and safety demands of a growing and diversifying population. Built decades ago, the current capitol structure suffers from outdated facilities, limited space for administrative expansion, and insufficient resilience against climate-related hazards such as typhoons, earthquakes, and flooding—risks that frequently affect this side of Mindoro Island. In response, the provincial government has initiated plans to construct a new 2-storey provincial capitol building within a newly designated government complex in Mamburao. The new structure is envisioned as a symbol of progress, institutional integrity, and service-oriented governance. It will house key executive and legislative offices, administrative departments, and public service counters, while also accommodating disaster-resilient infrastructure, efficient workflows, and sustainable design strategies reflective of the province’s agricultural and environmental character. The provincial government has commissioned an architect to lead the project from conceptual design to coordination with structural engineers, planners, and contractors. The goal is to deliver a modern, functional, and civic-minded government center that can serve the present needs of Occidental Mindoro’s citizens while anticipating future demands in governance, development planning, and community engagement. Following a series of planning sessions and consultations, the following spatial requirements for the 2400sqm building were identified:
1. The ground floor is accessed through 15m x 15m main lobby connected to the 15m x 375sqm atrium. To the left side of the atrium and lobby is the executive offices which has an area of 22.5m x 40m and to the left are the following:
1. circulation and support spaces - 135sqm
2. administrative offices - 427.5sqm
3. session hall - 337.5 sqm
2. On the second floor are the following spaces
1. governor’s office - 40.5m x 12m with an overlooking view of the people’s plaza
2. administrative offices - 19.5m x 34m on the right side of the governor’s office
3. circulation and support spaces - 135sqm on the northeastern side
4. hallway - 3m wide all around the atrium and connecting to the bridge going to the multilevel parking building
Site Features. The parcel allocated for the new provincial capitol building of Occidental Mindoro is along the Capitol Road and near the entrance of the provincial capitol complex. Oriented towards the north-west direction, the capitol road is the main thoroughfare of the capitol complex which measures 1.3 hectares. The capitol building is to be placed on the north-east side of the road facing the new people’s plaza on the other side. The building has a 60m frontage same with the plaza in its front. Its facade faces the SW direction. The area is relatively flat. The parcel for the capitol building has an allocated 50m x 3300sqm area, a corner lot bounded by a 12m road on its front and a 10m on its left side. A multilevel parking building is to be built on the opposite side of the 10m wide service road with a bridge that connects to the 2nd floor of the main capitol building. The parking building has a TGFA of 1,360sqm.
Design Objectives. The primary objective is to create a modern, resilient, and dignified 2-storey provincial capitol building that reflects the institutional identity and service-oriented mission of the Provincial Government of Occidental Mindoro. The design must support efficient administrative workflows, ensure accessibility and public engagement, and incorporate disaster-resilient features suited to the province’s climate risks. Special emphasis will be placed on organizing executive, legislative, and public service spaces around a central atrium, fostering openness and transparency. The building shall also establish a strong civic presence along Capitol Road, with strategic integration to the adjacent People’s Plaza and direct connection to the multilevel parking facility via a second-floor bridge, ensuring seamless circulation within the new capitol complex.

q: Which of the following is considered a safety lighting?
n: Twin-head emergency lamps are battery-backed units that switch on automatically during power failure to light egress paths, so they are safety lighting. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); NFPA 101, Sec. 7.9.

q: Where should a UFO emergency light be installed?
n: UFO-type (round, recessed or surface) emergency lights are installed on the ceiling to spread egress illumination widely. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR (Emergency Lighting); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Outline specifications are a deliverable under what design phase?
n: Outline specifications are part of the Design Development Phase deliverables, together with the developed drawings and the updated cost estimate. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Design Development Phase deliverables.

q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the building permit?
n: A Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) from the BFP is a prerequisite for the building permit. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSEC).

q: Which of the following BFP-issued documents is required for the occupancy permit?
n: A Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from the BFP is required for the certificate of occupancy and for business permits. Source: RA 9514 (Fire Code) 2019 RIRR, Rule 9 (FSIC).

q: Ideal type of door for closing and opening a commercial space unit.
n: A sectional (overhead) door closes a commercial unit securely. It opens upward in panels and needs no swing space. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8 (Overhead Doors); DASMA standards.

q: Standared wind speed used in commercial air curtains.
n: Commercial air curtains typically discharge air at about 9–11 m/s at the nozzle, enough to keep a seal across the doorway. Source: AMCA 220 (Air Curtain Units – Laboratory Methods of Testing); manufacturers' data.

q: A 1.20m diameter circular table can accommodate how many seats?
n: A round table about 1.20 m in diameter seats 4 comfortably, and up to 6 at about 600 mm per person. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Dining); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: Which construction system is most suitable for a manufacturing facility requiring fast construction, cost efficiency, and wide clear spans?
n: The PEB (Pre-Engineered Building) system is ideal for manufacturing facilities because it allows quick erection, reduced material waste, and large column-free spaces, making it more efficient than traditional systems like CIP (Cast-In-Place) or RCMF (Reinforced Concrete Moment Frame). Pre-engineered buildings (PEB) use factory-made steel frames and cladding that are bolted together quickly. They give wide clear spans at low cost, which suits factories and warehouses. Source: Allen & Iano, Fundamentals of Building Construction, Ch. 11 (Pre-engineered Metal Buildings); MBMA Metal Building Systems Manual.

q: What is the main purpose of using bubbledeck slabs in structural design?
n: Bubbledeck slabs incorporate hollow plastic balls within the concrete slab to eliminate non-structural concrete, significantly reducing the dead weight while maintaining structural strength and rigidity. BubbleDeck slabs put hollow plastic spheres in the slab to replace concrete that does no structural work. This cuts dead weight by about a third. Source: BubbleDeck Technical Manual; Ching, Building Structures Illustrated (Concrete Slabs).

q: Which type of waffle slab mold is typically used for achieving longer spans in structural applications?
n: Deeper waffle (dome) molds make deeper ribs and a stiffer slab, so it can span farther. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 4 (Waffle Slabs); ACI 318, Joist Construction.

q: What is the main advantage of a portal frame in low-rise buildings?
n: Portal frames have rigid beam-to-column joints, so they span widely without interior columns. That is the main reason they are used for low-rise sheds and halls. Source: Ching, Building Structures Illustrated (Rigid Frames); Schodek & Bechthold, Structures.

q: What is the connection point called where members meet in a space truss?
n: In a space truss, the members meet at nodes: spherical or plate connectors that join many members. Source: Schodek & Bechthold, Structures (Space Frames); Ching, Building Structures Illustrated.

s: Design Problem 1 – Single Detached in Semi-Exclusive Residences
q: What is the zone of the area?
n: "Semi-exclusive" points to R-2. Exclusive subdivisions are R-1. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (R-1 and R-2 Zones); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII.
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 1 – SINGLE DETACHED IN SEMI-EXCLUSIVE RESIDENCES

Design Problem. Mr. Shikahn is an Indian businessman who met Maria Santos, a 30-year old marketing manager from Dasmariñas, Cavite, at a Manila tech conference. They eventually got together and decided to marry in Maria’s hometown. Shikahn purchased a 0.0351ha interior lot adjacent a road facing commercial strip lot. He intends on making the Philippines their permanent home. Together they commissioned a three-storey house with 360-view on the 3rd floor. They were the one of the few first homeowners in the semi-exclusive residential area in General Trias, Cavite. Maria and Mr. Shikahn both love the outdoors so they wanted a home that connects them to nature. To achieve this, they listed the following requirements that their architect took note:
1. The ground floor building footprint maximizes open spaces. Instead of maximizing the allowable building footprint, 1.00m was added to the minimum required setbacks all around the building creating a wide looped open yard for the couple to enjoy.
1. Ground floor features a spacious living room at the front left, seamlessly flowing into a central dining area. The kitchen, located at the back right, connects to a cozy patio through sliding doors. A staircase and utility area occupy the right front, with a common toilet centrally positioned nearby.
2. The back patio features a cozy, covered space with outdoor seating, potted plants, and direct kitchen access through sliding doors, perfect for relaxed dining and social gatherings.
2. The second floor features a well-planned layout with two bedrooms and a family room. The master bedroom, situated at the back right, measures 5m x 4m and includes a private toilet and bath (2m x 2.5m), offering comfort and privacy. The secondary bedroom, located at the front left, is 4m x 4m, spacious enough for a queen-sized bed. Centrally positioned, the family room measures 4m x 5m, serving as a cozy gathering space. A common toilet and bath (2m x 2m) is conveniently placed in the hallway, accessible from both the family room and the secondary bedroom.
3. The third floor features a versatile entertainment room, a guest bedroom, and a spacious covered balcony. The entertainment room, located at the front, measures 5m x 6m, providing ample space for leisure and social activities. Adjacent to it, the guest room (4m x 4m) offers comfort and privacy for visitors. At the back, the covered balcony spans 4m x 6m, perfect for outdoor lounging, with seating and a partial garden setup. The balcony is accessible through sliding doors from the entertainment room, seamlessly blending indoor and outdoor spaces while offering panoramic views and a relaxing ambiance.
Site Features. A 7m wide, 8m long private road services the interior lot, also serving as its frontage. The private road connects to a 10.5m wide RROW oriented SW to NE. The lot is located on the NW side of the RROW, measuring 18.0m x 351sqm. The lot is separated from the RROW by an 8m deep 25m long commercial strip placed on both sides of the private road. Drainage naturally flows towards the north side at 2%.
Design Objectives. The three-storey residence shall blend Filipino and Indian cultural influences, reflecting the couple's shared identity and love for the outdoors. The design will feature open, airy spaces connecting indoor and outdoor living, with cultural elements like capiz windows and intricate patterns. Distinct family spaces will ensure privacy while common areas foster togetherness, creating a harmonious and welcoming home.

q: Which document outlines the legal framework, common areas, and management rules for a small residential development or condominium project?
n: The master deed establishes the overall legal structure of the project, including common areas, unit boundaries, and management provisions, making it essential for the operation of residential developments or condominiums. The master deed (with its declaration of restrictions) establishes a condominium. It defines the units, the common areas and the management rules. Source: RA 4726 (Condominium Act), Sec. 4; PD 957 IRR.

q: Where within a residential lot is xeriscaping most ideally located?
n: Xeriscaping is most ideally located in the front yard, where it enhances curb appeal and conserves water by using drought-tolerant plants in the most exposed and publicly visible area of the property. Xeriscaping (drought-tolerant landscaping) is often placed in the front yard, where it adds curb appeal and saves the most irrigation water. Source: US EPA WaterSense (Xeriscaping); Philippine Green Building Code (2015), Site.

s: Design Problem 1 – Single Detached in Semi-Exclusive Residences
q: What is the approximate difference in the elevation of the north and south corner of the lot?
n: If you correctly get the site layout, you can get the distance between north and south corner, which can be multiplied by 2%. Length from N-S = 26.54m x 0.02 = 0.53m. 26.54 m north–south x 0.02 = 0.53 m. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Grades and Slopes).

s: Design Problem 1 – Single Detached in Semi-Exclusive Residences
q: Considering vista and light, what is the distance between the public RROW crown to the rear property line?
n: Crown of the public RROW is usually the centerline since it is the highest point of the carriageway to efficiently shed or allow water to flow sidewards. Therefore, we must measure the distance from the centerline of the RROW to the rear property line. Distance = 5.25m (half of RROV) + 8m (length of the private road) + 19.5m (depth of the lot) = 32.75m. 5.25 m (half of the 10.5 m RROW, to the crown) + 8 m private road + 19.5 m lot depth = 32.75 m. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines, Criteria and Standards (Road Crown); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Light and Ventilation – Angular Plane).

q: In the computation of plumbing fees, one ____ is composed of 1 WC, 2 FD, 1 LAV, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head.
n: For plumbing permit fees, one "unit" is 1 water closet, 2 floor drains, 1 lavatory, 1 sink, 3 faucets and 1 shower head. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule II – Schedule of Fees (Plumbing Permit Fees).

s: Design Problem 3 – 3-Storey Retirement Home with Basement
q: How many tons of cement is required for the ground floor slab if the slab is 3000psi and 6” thick?
n: Let's first get the volume of the slab. We know that the footprint of the ground floor is 120sqm so we just multiply 120sqm x 0.125m = 15 cu.m.Take note that 3000PSI is Class B so 7.5 bags of cement /cu.m. Therefore 15cu.m. x 7.5 bags = 112.5 bags or 113 bags x 40kgs = 4,500kgs of cement. If we convert it to tons of cement, we divide it by 1000 so answer is 4.5 ton of cement. Per the exam key, 4.5 tons. The exam's solution uses 15 cu.m of slab and Class B mix at 7.5 bags of 40 kg per cu.m. Strictly, a 6" (0.15 m) slab over 120 sqm is 18 cu.m, or about 5.4 tons. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Proportions – Class B).
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 3 – 3-STOREY RETIREMENT HOME WITH BASEMENT

Design Problem. A semi-retired couple, both former small business owners in Metro Manila, decided to relocate to a quieter, more relaxed environment in Lipa, Batangas. With their children now living independently, the couple acquired a lot in a semi- exclusive subdivision where they plan to build their long-term residence. They envision a 3-storey home with a basement, designed not only for daily living but also for leisure and occasional visits, from grandchildren. Given their senior age, the couple requested the inclusion of a residential elevator to ensure comfort and accessibility across all levels of the home. A trusted family friend recommended an architect to lead the entire process—from conceptualization and architectural design to interior planning and contractor selection. The couple prefers a smooth, hands-off approach to the project. Through a series of architect-client meetings, the following requirements were identified:
1. On the ground level, an ample 3 slot parking area is provided on the front yard. To the left is a ramp going to the basement that houses the luxury cars owned by the couple. This also serves as an automobile workshop for them.
2. The ground floor of the 3-storey retirement home is composed of 10m x 120sqm footprint. The front setback is 1m deeper than the required for an R-3 basic lot. Side setbacks are measured 3m from both left and right corners.
1. Open plan living room with entertainment area measuring 10m x 50sqm.
2. The back portion is composed of 8.12sqm circulation area composed of the private elevator shaft and the stairs assembly. Adjacent to it is the maid’s quarters measuring 2.8m x 3.1m. The remaining portion is another open plan dining-kitchen scheme measuring 7.2m x 6m with a view of the northern corner of the lot where the katmon tree is located.
3. The 2nd floor is composed of 3 rooms - master bedroom, bedroom 1 and family room. Two 2.5m x 4.5m balconies are provided on the right side connected by a connecting balcony 1.5m x 3m in size. A 1.50m hallway connects the circulation area to the connecting balcony and serves the three rooms.
1. Master bedroom with an ensuite T&B and total area of 29.83sqm connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m balcony on the northern corner.
2. Bedroom 1 with a 4m x 24sqm dimensions facing the front yard. Adjacent to this is the family room with an area of 22.5sqm and connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m corner balcony.
4. The 3rd floor layout configuration is almost the same as the 2nd floor except that the bedroom 1, family room 1, balcony and a portion of the connecting balcony are now enclosed and serves as a large workshop area measuring 10m wide x 60sqm.
1. Bedroom with an ensuite T&B and total area of 29.83sqm connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m balcony on the northern corner.
2. A 1.50m x 7.20m hallways serves the three spaces.
Site Features. The lot is an irregularly shaped land along the 12m-wide Toledo Road. With a 16m-wide frontage, the sides measure 18m on left side and 18.25m on the right side. The rear side is 19m and is oriented N 61.13° E. The ground slopes down at 3% towards the SW side. Located in a high-density residential subzone A with a minimum density of 101 du/ha, the land value of the lot is already at 15,000php per sqm. Scattered across the property are various scraps and debris, including wood pieces, old fencing, and discarded materials. A few small shrubs and weeds are present along the edges, and there are no significant structures on the site except for a katmon tree on the northernmost corner of the lot. The land appears to have been unused for some time and would benefit from basic clearing and maintenance.
Design Objectives. The project aims to design a 3-storey residence with a basement for a semi-retired couple seeking a comfortable, low-maintenance home in Lipa, Batangas. The house must support aging-in-place with features like a residential elevator and an accessible layout across all levels, including a basement workshop and car storage, open-plan living spaces, private bedrooms, and a top-floor creative workspace. The design should respond to the lot’s irregular shape, slight slope, and existing Katmon tree, while ensuring functional zoning, natural light, and a seamless, hands-off process guided by the architect from concept to construction.

s: Design Problem 3 – 3-Storey Retirement Home with Basement
q: If the ensuite T&B of the master bedroom is 15% of the bedroom area, what is the required window opening area in square meters of the T&B?
n: If you get the layout correct, you should come up with a master bedroom area of 29.83sqm. Therefore, the T&B area is 4.47sqm and the required window opening is 0.22sqm. T&B = 15% x 29.83 sqm = 4.47 sqm. Its window must be at least 1/20 of the floor area: 4.47 / 20 = 0.22 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 808 (Window Openings).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 3 – 3-STOREY RETIREMENT HOME WITH BASEMENT

Design Problem. A semi-retired couple, both former small business owners in Metro Manila, decided to relocate to a quieter, more relaxed environment in Lipa, Batangas. With their children now living independently, the couple acquired a lot in a semi- exclusive subdivision where they plan to build their long-term residence. They envision a 3-storey home with a basement, designed not only for daily living but also for leisure and occasional visits, from grandchildren. Given their senior age, the couple requested the inclusion of a residential elevator to ensure comfort and accessibility across all levels of the home. A trusted family friend recommended an architect to lead the entire process—from conceptualization and architectural design to interior planning and contractor selection. The couple prefers a smooth, hands-off approach to the project. Through a series of architect-client meetings, the following requirements were identified:
1. On the ground level, an ample 3 slot parking area is provided on the front yard. To the left is a ramp going to the basement that houses the luxury cars owned by the couple. This also serves as an automobile workshop for them.
2. The ground floor of the 3-storey retirement home is composed of 10m x 120sqm footprint. The front setback is 1m deeper than the required for an R-3 basic lot. Side setbacks are measured 3m from both left and right corners.
1. Open plan living room with entertainment area measuring 10m x 50sqm.
2. The back portion is composed of 8.12sqm circulation area composed of the private elevator shaft and the stairs assembly. Adjacent to it is the maid’s quarters measuring 2.8m x 3.1m. The remaining portion is another open plan dining-kitchen scheme measuring 7.2m x 6m with a view of the northern corner of the lot where the katmon tree is located.
3. The 2nd floor is composed of 3 rooms - master bedroom, bedroom 1 and family room. Two 2.5m x 4.5m balconies are provided on the right side connected by a connecting balcony 1.5m x 3m in size. A 1.50m hallway connects the circulation area to the connecting balcony and serves the three rooms.
1. Master bedroom with an ensuite T&B and total area of 29.83sqm connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m balcony on the northern corner.
2. Bedroom 1 with a 4m x 24sqm dimensions facing the front yard. Adjacent to this is the family room with an area of 22.5sqm and connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m corner balcony.
4. The 3rd floor layout configuration is almost the same as the 2nd floor except that the bedroom 1, family room 1, balcony and a portion of the connecting balcony are now enclosed and serves as a large workshop area measuring 10m wide x 60sqm.
1. Bedroom with an ensuite T&B and total area of 29.83sqm connected to a 2.5m x 4.5m balcony on the northern corner.
2. A 1.50m x 7.20m hallways serves the three spaces.
Site Features. The lot is an irregularly shaped land along the 12m-wide Toledo Road. With a 16m-wide frontage, the sides measure 18m on left side and 18.25m on the right side. The rear side is 19m and is oriented N 61.13° E. The ground slopes down at 3% towards the SW side. Located in a high-density residential subzone A with a minimum density of 101 du/ha, the land value of the lot is already at 15,000php per sqm. Scattered across the property are various scraps and debris, including wood pieces, old fencing, and discarded materials. A few small shrubs and weeds are present along the edges, and there are no significant structures on the site except for a katmon tree on the northernmost corner of the lot. The land appears to have been unused for some time and would benefit from basic clearing and maintenance.
Design Objectives. The project aims to design a 3-storey residence with a basement for a semi-retired couple seeking a comfortable, low-maintenance home in Lipa, Batangas. The house must support aging-in-place with features like a residential elevator and an accessible layout across all levels, including a basement workshop and car storage, open-plan living spaces, private bedrooms, and a top-floor creative workspace. The design should respond to the lot’s irregular shape, slight slope, and existing Katmon tree, while ensuring functional zoning, natural light, and a seamless, hands-off process guided by the architect from concept to construction.

s: Design Problem 3 – 3-Storey Retirement Home with Basement
q: What is the approximate number of gypsyum boards for the ceiling of the hallway at the 3rd floor?
n: The area of the hallway at the 3rd floor is 10.8sqm and the standard size of gypsum board is 1.2 x 2.4m = 2.88sqm. Therefore, the number of gypsum boards = 3.75pcs or 4 pcs. 10.8 sqm / 2.88 sqm per board = 3.75, so 4 boards. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Ceiling Boards).

q: Where is the best location for a lanai?
n: A lanai at the northeast corner gets morning sun and the cooler northeast breezes, and is shaded from the hot afternoon sun. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building (Orientation); PAGASA climate data.

q: What type of Portland Cement is ideal for massive concrete construction?
n: Type IV (low-heat) Portland cement generates the least heat of hydration. That limits thermal cracking in massive pours such as dams and thick foundations. Source: ASTM C150 (Portland Cement Types); Kosmatka et al., Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures (PCA).

q: What concrete class is used for columns and slabs?
n: Structural members such as columns, beams and suspended slabs commonly use Class A concrete (1:2:4, about 21 MPa). Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Concrete Classes); DPWH Standard Specifications, Item 405.

q: A rope used to control a lifted load's swing or rotation during lifting.
n: A tag line is a rope attached to a lifted load to help ground personnel guide, control, or stabilize it, especially in windy or tight conditions where the load might rotate or sway. A tag line is a rope tied to a suspended load. A worker uses it to control swing and rotation during lifting. Source: DOLE OSHS (Construction Safety – Rigging); ASME B30.5 (Mobile Cranes).

q: What shall be the bend diameter if the rebar size is 16mm?
n: For 10mm to 25mm rebars, the bend diameter shall be 6 times the bar diameter. Therefore, for 16mm rebar the bend diameter shall be 96mm or 4 inches. Standard hooks on bars from 10 mm through 25 mm need an inside bend diameter of 6 bar diameters. For 16 mm that is 6 × 16 = 96 mm, about 4 in. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 425.3.1 (Minimum Inside Bend Diameters); ACI 318.

q: In pitched-roof construction, what is the horizontal member that connects opposing rafters at their base to prevent them from spreading apart?
n: A tie beam is a horizontal structural member at the base of a roof truss or rafter set, designed to resist outward thrust and maintain the stability of the roof structure. In pitched roofs, the tie beam (or ceiling joist) joins the feet of opposing rafters. It holds them in tension so they cannot spread. Collar ties sit higher up. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 6 (Rafter Framing).

q: Which of the following is a volume quantity?
n: Building bulk is a volume, the three-dimensional envelope a building may occupy. OFB, development controls and BHL are faces, rules or heights. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Building Bulk and Building Envelope).

q: Which test is conducted on-site to determine the optimal moisture content and maximum dry density of soil for compaction purposes?
n: The Proctor test measures how well soil compacts at various moisture levels, helping ensure a stable base for construction. It is essential in site development for roads, foundations, and backfill areas. The Proctor compaction test finds a soil's optimum moisture content and maximum dry density. That sets the target for field compaction. Source: ASTM D698 / D1557 (Standard and Modified Proctor); Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering.

q: What is the primary purpose of using hub and tack in site development?
o: To serve as erosion control points
To indicate precise reference points for layout
n: Hub and tack are used to establish exact reference points for elevation, alignment, and location during construction layout, ensuring accurate transfer of plans onto the site. Hubs (stakes) with tacks driven into their tops mark precise survey reference points for setting out the layout. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Construction Staking); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 1.

q: In a CARI policy, who is theinsurer who assumes the financial risk in case of loss or damage during the construction period?
n: Under a Contractor's All Risk Insurance (CARI) policy, the insurer, the insurance company, assumes the financial risk of loss or damage during construction. Source: Insurance Code of the Philippines (PD 612 as amended by RA 10607); UAP SPP Doc. 301 (Insurance).

q: What is the main basis for determining payment amounts in a construction progress billing?
n: The schedule of values is a detailed cost breakdown of a construction project, serving as the primary reference for calculating payments based on the percentage of work completed during each billing cycle. Progress billings are based on the schedule of values, which breaks the contract sum into work items. Payment is based on the percentage completed on each item. Source: AIA G702/G703 (Application and Certificate for Payment); UAP SPP Doc. 301.

q: Which of the following is an example of a floating floor system that uses interlocking edges for installation without adhesive or mechanical fasteners?
n: Click-lock flooring is designed with interlocking edges that snap together, allowing it to float above the subfloor without glue or fasteners. Click-lock flooring (laminate, engineered or vinyl) has interlocking edges that snap together. It floats on the underlay without glue or nails. Source: NWFA Installation Guidelines (Floating Floors); manufacturers' installation guides.

q: Which type of tile features patterns made by inlaid colors rather than surface glaze?
n: Encaustic tiles are made by layering different colors of clay into patterns, resulting in designs that won't wear off over time. Encaustic tiles get their pattern from colored clays inlaid into the body, not from a surface glaze. The pattern lasts as the tile wears. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Encaustic Tile); TCNA Handbook.

q: Why was popcorn ceiling originally used in residential construction?
o: To hide imperfections and absorb sound
To make ceilings easier to clean
n: Popcorn ceilings or stipple ceiling were popular for their ability to conceal surface flaws and provide sound dampening, reducing the need for perfectly smooth finishes and improving acoustic performance. Popcorn (acoustic) ceiling texture was sprayed on to hide surface defects cheaply and to absorb some sound. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Acoustic Ceiling Texture); US EPA (asbestos-era popcorn ceilings).

q: What is the standard projection of kitchen countertop lip?
n: Countertops commonly overhang the cabinet face by about 1 to 1.5 in, with 1.25 in typical. That protects the cabinet doors from drips. Source: NKBA Kitchen Planning Guidelines; Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI, Countertops).

q: Which of the following spaces typically requires the use of cement backer board behind wall tiles?
n: Backer board is used in wet areas like showers to provide a moisture-resistant and stable surface for tile installation, preventing water damage and mold growth behind the tiles. Shower areas need cement backer board behind the tiles. Unlike gypsum board, it does not deteriorate when wet. Source: TCNA Handbook (Wet Area Installations); ANSI A118.9 (Cementitious Backer Units).
